extra.message: User-controlled search query is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe. The isSQLInjectionAttempt/isAccessingFlagsTable checks are bypassable filters, not escaping, so arbitrary SQL can be injected (e.g. UNION SELECT).

The 'status' body field is concatenated into a raw SQL string (AND o.status = '${status}') and executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe without parameterization, allowing SQL injection by an authenticated user.
The X-Forwarded-For header value ('ip') is concatenated into a raw INSERT statement without escaping (only userAgent/path are escaped). This allows SQL injection via a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header.

The 'author' query parameter is concatenated into a raw SQL string (WHERE r.author = '${authorFilter}') executed via better-sqlite3 db.exec/db.prepare. This is a second-order SQL injection where attacker-controlled review author data flows into the query.

The 'file' query parameter is joined to the documents directory with path.join without any traversal sanitization, then read via readFile. An unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files (e.g. file=../../prisma/dev.db) or list directories via the 'list'/'path' parameters.

The 'screenshotUrl' request field is passed directly to fetch() without validation, allowing SSRF against internal resources (the request also carries an X-Internal-Request: true header, enabling access to internal-only endpoints).

The user-supplied 'mcpServerUrl' is passed to fetch() without validation. The backend acts as a proxy, enabling SSRF to internal networks and indirect prompt injection from malicious MCP tool responses.

libxmljs.parseXmlString is called with noent:true and dtdload:true, enabling external entity resolution. An authenticated admin can supply XML with a DOCTYPE/ENTITY to read arbitrary local files (e.g. flag-xxe.txt) via XXE.

GET /api/orders/[id] fetches any order by id without checking order.userId against the authenticated user, returning the customer's email and full delivery address (the flag is set but the data is still returned). IDOR allowing disclosure of other users' PII.

GET /api/wishlists/[id] returns any wishlist (including the owner's email address) without enforcing ownership. The userId check only sets a flag after the fact; the object and owner PII are still returned to any authenticated user.

POST /api/user/support-access accepts an arbitrary 'email' in the body and creates a support access token for that user (no ownership/role check). Combined with /api/auth/support-login, an attacker can mint a login token for any account, including ADMIN, achieving full account takeover.

POST /api/live/stream is protected by withAuth instead of withAdminAuth, so any authenticated (non-admin) user can change the live video broadcast. The GET handler likewise exposes the RTMP stream key to any authenticated user.

Order status update relies solely on the Referer header to distinguish admin dashboard requests and uses no CSRF token. An attacker can forge/omit the Referer, causing a state-changing request to be treated as cross-site (CSRF) and the auth cookie is sent automatically.

Review content (user-controlled via POST /api/products/[id]/reviews) is assigned to innerHTML and any <script> tags are re-created and executed. This is a stored XSS affecting any user who views the product page.
The user's 'bio' field (set via POST /api/user/profile) is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing stored XSS on the profile page.

Visitor IP addresses (sourced from the unvalidated X-Forwarded-For header and stored via /api/tracking) are rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML. An attacker who injects HTML/JS into X-Forwarded-For achieves stored XSS on the admin analytics page.

The 'screenshotContent' returned by the server (from an SSRF fetch of a user-supplied URL) is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, enabling XSS via attacker-controlled remote content.
The 'redirect' query parameter is taken from the URL and assigned to window.location.href after login with no validation, allowing an open redirect to an arbitrary external or javascript: URL.
The JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded value 'secret'. An attacker who knows this default can forge valid tokens with any id/role (including ADMIN), defeating all token-based auth.

decodeJWT only base64-decodes and JSON.parses the JWT payload and never verifies the signature. The role check trusts this unverified payload, so anyone can forge an ADMIN token to pass the middleware protecting /monitoring/internal-status.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (hashMD5). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, enabling fast offline cracking and rainbow-table attacks on the password store.
The login handler logs the plaintext password (and a flag value) for every login attempt via logger.warn. Credentials are written to logs/app.log and exposed through the SIEM log viewer.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The signup body schema (lib/validation/schemas/auth.ts) accepts a 'role' field with .passthrough(). The handler assigns body.role directly to the created user, so anyone can register with role ADMIN and gain administrative privileges.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Hardcoded SIEM credentials (root/admin) are used to authenticate to the log viewer. The resulting siem_session cookie is set to a fixed value 'authenticated', so the log endpoint can also be accessed by simply forging that cookie.

A hardcoded backdoor token 'dbg_8f3a7c91e2b4d6a05e21' is compared in plain text to authorize the diagnostic endpoint, which discloses an internal flag. The credential is embedded in source and trivially guessable/leakable.

GET /api/flags (and /api/flags/[slug]) return the full Flag records, including the flag values, to unauthenticated users. This exposes the entire CTF answer key / sensitive data without authentication.

The export endpoint returns raw error messages, stack traces, and system diagnostics (Node version, environment, internal flag) to the client on error. ALLOWED_USER_FIELDS also includes 'password', permitting export of the password hash.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Password reset tokens are generated as MD5(email + timestamp) where the timestamp is derived from a 'requestedAt' value returned in the same response. This is predictable and allows an attacker to generate valid reset tokens and take over accounts.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: Gift card codes are generated by a deterministic LCG seeded with the creation timestamp (createdAt.getTime()), making codes predictable and guessable by an attacker who knows the creation time.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: Share tokens use AES-256-CBC without any integrity/MAC. decryptShareToken throws on invalid padding, exposing a padding-oracle that an attacker can exploit to recover plaintexts, and the hardcoded fallback key is in source.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The order total is taken directly from the client-supplied 'total' field and persisted without server-side recomputation, allowing price manipulation during checkout (client-side enforcement of a server-side value).

cwe: CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security

extra.message: Coupon validation (check-then-act on coupon.usedCount) is separated from the increment by an artificial delay, creating a TOCTOU race window. Concurrent requests can exceed maxUses and reuse a single coupon.

cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization

extra.message: A hardcoded broadcast stream key and RTMP ingest URL are stored in source and exposed to any authenticated user through GET /api/live/stream, allowing unauthorized access to the live broadcast.

The MCP session secret ('oopssec-internal-agent') is hardcoded and used as the sole authorization gate for the privileged get_compliance_report tool. Anyone who learns this static header value can call the restricted tool.
